title: Polynomial accuracy dependence for sublinear LIS estimation
formal: With adaptive random access to a length-\(n\) array, can the length of its longest increasing subsequence be estimated within additive error \(\varepsilon n\) in time polynomial in \(\log n\) and \(1/\varepsilon\)?

import_provenance.original_title: Polynomial accuracy dependence for sublinear LIS estimation
import_provenance.original_statement: With adaptive random access to an array of length n, can its longest increasing subsequence length be estimated to additive error εn in time polynomial in log n and 1/ε? Saks and Seshadhri achieved polylogarithmic dependence on n but exponential dependence on inverse accuracy.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: This is an editorial continuation of Saks–Seshadhri. Adaptivity is essential: known nonadaptive lower bounds rule out the stated polynomial dependence simultaneously on log n and 1/ε.
